title: Can local text embeddings detect agent failures?
lines: Team G04 · NYCU Data Mining HW2
284 real SWE-agent runs from SWE-bench Lite
MiniLM logs + CodeBERT patches, computed locally
Frozen encoders lose to simple numeric controls
notes: Task-end failure screening. No generated trajectories or new LLM API calls. Official resolution labels are the target. Source: Dataset/evaluation_results.json. Full author list and student IDs appear in the report.

title: The decision is whether a completed run needs review
lines: Normal reference: 54 officially resolved tasks
Failure label: 230 unresolved tasks (81.0%)
Errors, large patches and high cost do not prove failure
Failure is common here, which limits the anomaly framing
notes: Category 4: Text / Logs. Labels do not establish deception, reward hacking or false completion. No prefix prediction or autonomous release has been tested. SWE-bench and SWE-agent sources are in Paper/custom.bib.

title: Training-only analysis shows overlapping behavior
lines: EDA uses outer fold 0 training rows only
32 successful and 138 failed training runs
Long tails motivate log1p and robust scaling
Remove duplicated command count from numeric features
notes: No held-out row enters these boxplots. Numeric control has 23 columns, including 4 binary flags. The test-string flag is patch-wide and the command heuristic is noisy. Source: Paper/figures/v2/eda and v2_stats.tex.

title: Local encoders preserve more of the recorded text
lines: MiniLM: chunk logs, average within and across steps
CodeBERT: chunk diff hunks, pool token representations
Normalize 384-D log and 768-D patch vectors
T2: mean distance to k nearby successful training runs
notes: Encoders remain frozen. Log chunks:224 tokens,32 overlap. Patch chunks:480 tokens,64 overlap. Log and patch cosine distances have equal weight. k in {1,3,5}; only successful training rows form the reference. Pooling loses ordering and does not verify correctness.

title: Every method shares five outer folds
lines: Approx. 60% training, 20% validation, 20% outer test
Validation selects model and threshold; never fits weights
Choose recall under validation FPR <=20%
284 out-of-fold predictions per model and seed
Prior data inspection makes this exploratory evaluation
notes: Only around 32 successful training and 10 successful validation runs per fold. Empirical validation FPR is not a test guarantee. Shared repositories remain; additional held-out-repository sensitivity is limited. Deterministic methods run once, random methods have seeds42,123,456.

title: Numeric controls outperform the embedding detector
lines: Seed 42 pooled counts; no independent deployment test
ECOD minus T2 balanced accuracy: +0.176
Paired conditional 95% interval: [0.114, 0.240]
notes: All numbers derive from main_results.csv and bootstrap_ci.csv. Bootstrap resamples paired OOF instances within class2000times; shared training folds limit interpretation. Conditional residual is a secondary comparison. No method meets all operational gates.

title: The confusion matrices expose the missed failures
lines: T2: 179 of 230 failures receive no alert
Only 40 of 219 unflagged runs actually succeed
Better numeric scores still leave many failures unflagged
notes: Rows are actual success/failure. Columns are no alert/alert. Cell text is raw count; color is row fraction. T2 TN40FP14FN179TP51;ECOD TN47FP7FN128TP102;conditional TN44FP10FN107TP123. Prediction absence of alert is not a correctness guarantee.

title: Patch vectors help, but dual-channel averaging hurts
lines: Numeric kNN: balanced accuracy 0.641
Patch-only encoder: 0.594
Dual encoder: 0.481; log-only: 0.456
H1 unsupported; patch addition helps logs, not patch-only
notes: All use kNN and validation model selection. Distances differ across representations, so this comparison includes geometry. Patch embeddings may encode surface similarity rather than functional correctness. Equal averaging is one tested fusion rule, not proof all text encoders fail.

title: Contamination does not show a consistent penalty
lines: Fixed reference size; training failures replace successes
Freeze each clean fold’s chosen k and threshold
Also report validation-only recalibration
Zero-contamination reproduces the primary detector
notes: Corrected after detecting a mismatched k=3 control in the earlier v2 draft. Fitting IDs and exact replacement fractions are archived. Three replacement seeds. H3 is not established if effects are small or nonmonotonic. Source:contamination_fitting_ids.json and ablation_contamination.csv.

title: Near-normal vectors can still describe failed patches
lines: FP django-13230: score .11276, threshold .10865
FN sympy-12454: score .02483, threshold .07315
Boundary FP sympy-24213: margin +.00018
Distances identify similarity, not the semantic cause
notes: Full IDs and raw SHA256s are in case_studies.json. Nearest reference log/patch distances respectively .20290/.00655, .04656/.00311, .14414/.00251. The saved leave-one-out values use a fixed nearest reference, not full kNN rescoring; do not call them complete score attribution.

title: These detectors cannot justify automatic release
lines: No model meets the predeclared practical gates
Next: fresh agent runs and task-conditioned evidence
Encoding 284 runs took about 895 seconds on CPU
All five member contributions remain pending confirmation
notes: Gates:recall>=90%,FPR<=20%,unflagged success>=80%,coverage>=5%. Encoder memory reported ~1.19GiB by extractor profiling; not a whole-process-tree memory guarantee. Actual live rehearsal and E3 upload remain outstanding. AI assistance and all five author IDs appear in the report.
